factors.label: Water volume
factors.rule: 0 at 100,000 m³ rising (log scale) to 1 at 100,000,000 m³
factors.why: More water means a bigger, longer-reaching flood. On this scale 1 and 10 million m³ (the low/medium and medium/high class limits of Kougkoulos et al. 2018) sit at 0.33 and 0.67.
factors.source: Volume from area by Huggel et al. 2002, V = 0.104·A^1.42 (https://doi.org/10.1139/t01-099); classes: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2017.10.083

method.formula: score = 100 x size x likelihood; size and likelihood are weighted means of their factors' 0-1 scores
method.hindsight: Each replay entry uses only seasons up to as_of_season and the 2011-2015 DEM.
method.disclaimer: Screening score for prioritising attention, not a probability of failure.
